rootCause: BEFORE: the request chain was serialised. The bundle was parsed, then the app asked for the joint manifest, then the body manifest, then the body meshes; the first body stage was the full grouped skeleton (598 KB), and background stages competed with the first frame.

AFTER: the HTML preloads the two manifests, the baked environment and the two first-stage meshes, so every startup request begins at ~0.26 s and all of them finish by ~0.98 s; the first frame is a delivery-only proxy (2 body draw calls, 27,760 triangles, 219 KB brotli); background preloads are deferred until after the first frame.

REMAINING critical path at 4x: bundle download 0.25-0.99 s (210 KB brotli) -> module evaluation ~0.13 s -> app construct ~1.3 s -> content validation 47 ms -> first shot applied 17 ms -> shader compilation ~0.36 s -> first draw ~0.08 s -> first meaningful 3D ~2.1-2.5 s.

Tested and rejected: fetchPriority=low on the first-stage meshes so the bundle would win the link. The bundle still finished at ~0.99 s (the emulated Fast 4G link is saturated either way) and first 3D did not improve (2353 / 2543 ms vs 2133 ms). Not kept.

methodologyFix.problem: The Step 12 drag harness moved the pointer along a fixed sine path. That path drives the hinge into its 0 deg / 145 deg limits: for 53% of the steps the pose did not change, so the render loop correctly rendered nothing, and the harness counted those idle gaps as frame intervals and as input latency.
methodologyFix.symptom: frame interval max 734 ms, raw input latency p95 637 ms, 28.8 fps - all measurement artefact, confirmed by a trace with no main-thread task over 12 ms in the same window.
methodologyFix.fix: Closed-loop drag: each step reads the current angle and moves the pointer along the axis that drives the joint towards a 25-120 deg target (period 2.6 s), so every step changes the pose. unchangedStepFraction is recorded with every result and is 0.

perFrameCost.note: render CPU = first gl.clear to the end of the frame callback (three render + label update), same closed-loop drag, same build

hotPathAudit.allocations: no per-frame Vector3/Matrix allocation left on the drag path (scratch vectors in LabelSystem, scratch Matrix3 in anchorLabelDirectionWorld); minor GC 14-21 ms per 8-10 s window, no major GC
hotPathAudit.layoutReads: no getBoundingClientRect on the drag path (canvas rect and stage size cached, invalidated on resize/scroll/fullscreen); the tracer reports no forced style/layout stacks
hotPathAudit.domWrites: 17.4 mutations per rendered frame, all necessary: label transforms and leader-line endpoints (~13), slider fill/thumb/readout/aria-valuenow (~4). Change-only writes are already in place (setStyle/setAttr compare before writing).
hotPathAudit.drawCalls: 68 at hinge.try: 30 elbow meshes, 30 dimmed body groups, 8 overlay draws; 12 unique materials; 183k triangles; nothing out of frustum

whyCpu4xMissesTheTarget.measured: p50 is at vsync (16.7-17.2 ms) but p95 is 45-50 ms: about every 20th frame takes 3 vsync intervals.
eliminated: not JS work volume: hiding the whole dimmed body (30 fewer draw calls, 180k fewer triangles) did not improve fps or p95; hiding the overlays did not; hiding the UI panel did not; every difference was inside the +/-6 fps run-to-run spread of this machine
not pixels: DPR 1.5 vs 1.25 vs 1.0 measured 44.8-47.9 / 46.2-47.9 / 45.7-47.4 fps over 3 runs each - no trend

not the CPU-throttle emulation by itself: a style-only control page holds 60 fps at 4x, and a WebGL control page with 68 draw calls at the same canvas size (618x1372) also holds 60 fps at 4x (p95 21.4 ms)

not a single long task: the tracer finds at most 1-2 frames over 30 ms per 8-10 s window, and inside them the time sits in a blocking GL call (uniformMatrix4fv 27 ms), i.e. the main thread waiting on the driver rather than running our code
whyCpu4xMissesTheTarget.conclusion: On this hardware the 4x-CPU emulated phone profile loses roughly every 20th frame to the throttled main thread plus the GL/compositor handshake, and the loss does not respond to any reduction of application work. The 4x figure is reported as measured: the p95 <= 22 ms target is NOT met on that profile. It is met at 1x and 2x. This is emulation, not a device certification.

explore.rootCauseFixedInStep12R: Label occlusion raycasts ran on every frame while the camera moved (getVertexPosition 524 ms per 8 s at 4x). Occlusion testing is now deferred while the camera moves and runs once it settles (CAMERA_SETTLE_MS 180 plus a settle timer).
explore.remaining: the same platform-level frame loss as the drag at 4x; 60 fps at 2x
